problem: Prior LLM-based zero-shot ObjectNav methods (L3MVN, ESC) prompt the LLM with only the category names of objects near each frontier and ask it to output a frontier probability directly. This discards scene context such as spatial and functional relations and gives unexplainable, weak decisions. Separately, modular ObjectNav pipelines commit irreversibly to the first detected goal instance, so a false-positive detection causes episode failure.
motivation: Zero-shot, open-vocabulary ObjectNav needs an LLM to do commonsense reasoning. The LLM cannot see the scene, so the representation it is given is the bottleneck: a structured hierarchical 3D scene graph of objects, groups and rooms with relation edges is both richer and LLM-friendly. Detectors in cluttered homes often produce false positives, and a scene-context prior can be used to verify a detected goal before committing to it.
key_idea: Build an online hierarchical 3D scene graph (objects/groups/rooms with LLM-proposed, VLM/geometry-pruned relation edges) and score frontiers by prompting an LLM with a hierarchical chain-of-thought over subgraphs. The same subgraph scores are reused to accumulate credibility for detected goals and reject false positives.
insight:
Most of the SR gain over prior SOTA comes from two sources: scene-graph-guided frontier scoring and false-positive rejection. With re-perception removed, SG-Nav-LLaMA falls to 36.5 SR on MP3D / 49.6 on HM3D / 41.9 on RoboTHOR (Table 2), which is roughly on par with OpenFMNav/VLFM. Adding RP gives +3.6/+4.3/+5.4 SR but only +1.0/+1.2/+1.1 SPL, since the agent still walks to the candidate to verify it. Removing both SG and RP (random frontier) drops MP3D SR to 25.7, so the graph-based LLM scoring is worth about +10.8 SR over random frontier selection. Within the graph:
- Relation edges matter (nodes-only 38.0 vs full 40.1), with short-range edges more useful than long-range ones (39.0 without short vs 39.5 without long).
- Group nodes help more than room nodes (39.4 vs 39.0 when added alone to 38.3).
- Hierarchical CoT beats flattening the graph into text (36.5 → 40.2).
LLaMA-7B and GPT-4 give nearly identical results (40.1 vs 40.2 on MP3D), which suggests perception and representation, not LLM strength, is the limiting factor.
method: Online hierarchical 3D scene graph: object nodes come from ConceptGraphs-style online open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation (per-frame detection/segmentation merged into 3D instances with category + confidence). Room nodes come from the same segmenter prompted with room types. Group nodes are formed iteratively from edge-connected object pairs whose categories appear in an LLM-generated related-category dictionary (e.g., table–chair, bed–nightstand).

Inter-level (affiliation) edges: an object is linked to a room if its point-cloud instance mask lies inside the room mask; a group is linked to a room if all its objects belong to that room. There are no group–object edges and no intra-level group/room edges.

Incremental dense edge proposal: the m newly registered object nodes are densely paired with all m+n nodes. All m(m+n) pairs go into a single batched JSON prompt asking for the most likely relationship (next to / above / opposite to / ...), which the paper argues reduces LLM cost from O(m(m+n)) to O(m).

Edge pruning: an edge is short-range if some RGB frame contains both objects; short-range edges are verified by asking LLaVA-1.6 (Mistral-7B) whether the relation exists. Long-range edges are kept only if the line between the objects is unobstructed and parallel to a room wall, and both objects belong to the same room node.

Hierarchical CoT subgraph scoring: each subgraph is an object node plus its parent nodes and directly connected objects. A 4-step prompt chain (predict object–goal distance → ask questions about object and goal → answer them from the subgraph's nodes/edges → summarize into a subgraph–goal distance) produces the distance d, and P_sub = 1/d.

Frontier selection + local planning: an 800×800 BEV occupancy map at 0.05 m gives the frontiers. Each frontier is scored P_fro_i = Σ_j P_sub_j / D_ij (D_ij = distance from the frontier center to the subgraph's central object), the highest-scoring frontier is chosen, and the Fast Marching Method plans the low-level actions. The LLM summarizes the 3 subgraphs nearest the chosen frontier as an explanation.

Graph-based re-perception: once a goal is detected, the agent approaches it and observes it from multiple views, accumulating S_k = C_k · Σ_j P_sub_j / D_j (C_k is the detector confidence). The goal is accepted if the cumulative score reaches S_thres = 0.8 within N_max = 10 observations; otherwise it is discarded and exploration resumes.

setting.backbone: Frozen LLM: LLaMA-7B (SG-Nav-LLaMA) or GPT-4-0613 (SG-Nav-GPT). Frozen LLaVA-1.6 (Mistral-7B) verifies short-range edges. ConceptGraphs-style open-vocab 3D instance segmentation (2D VLM + vision foundation model) handles perception. FBE + Fast Marching Method handle path planning.
setting.model_size: 7B LLM (LLaMA variant) or GPT-4 (undisclosed); 7B VLM for edge verification
setting.training_data: none (training-free); the related-category dictionary for group nodes is generated by an LLM
setting.observation: egocentric posed RGB-D (640×480, camera 0.90 m high, horizontal), depth range 1.5–10 m
setting.action_space: high-level frontier selection; low-level move_forward 0.25 m / turn_left / turn_right 30° / stop via FMM planner; max 500 steps
setting.privileged: none beyond agent pose (posed RGB-D input)

The CoT ablation (Table 5) reports the full model as 40.2/16.0 on MP3D (the GPT numbers), while the other ablations use 40.1 (LLaMA), so the ablation backbone is inconsistent. Per-category SR on MP3D and edge-construction timing appear only in figures (Fig. 4, Fig. 5), without numbers. The success distance d_s is not stated.
results: SG-Nav-GPT reaches 40.2 SR / 16.0 SPL on MP3D val, 54.0 / 24.9 on HM3D val and 47.5 / 24.0 on RoboTHOR val. It beats the strongest zero-shot baselines in SR: OpenFMNav (37.2 / 52.5 / 44.1) and VLFM (36.2 / 52.4 / 42.3). On MP3D it also beats the supervised SemExp (36.0 SR) and PONI (31.8 SR). SPL gains are small, and VLFM keeps a clearly higher HM3D SPL (30.3 vs 24.9). The LLaMA-7B variant is within 0.2 SR of GPT-4 everywhere.
limitations: Relies on a non-end-to-end, frame-merged 2D-to-3D open-vocabulary instance segmentation. Failure cases are perception errors (shelf mistaken for cabinet, goal not detected) and LLM commonsense misguidance. The paper handles only object-goal navigation.

SPL barely improves and trails VLFM on HM3D: re-perception adds path length because the agent must approach and multi-view verify candidates. The headline '>10% SR' claim holds against ESC/L3MVN, but the margin over the paper's own strongest baselines (OpenFMNav, VLFM) is only about +1.5 to +3.4 SR.

Heavy LLM usage: 4 CoT prompts per subgraph per step plus edge proposals and VLM edge checks. The paper gives no end-to-end runtime or API cost, only the relative edge-generation speed figure. Group formation uses a small hand-listed, LLM-generated related-category dictionary.
